Plot a tessellation map with optional boundary, seeds, and features

Source: R/plotting.R
plot_tessellation_map.Rd

Builds a layered ggplot2 map of the cells, with optional overlays of a study boundary, seed points and other features. Requires the ggplot2 package.

Usage

plot_tessellation_map(
  tessellation_sf,
  boundary = NULL,
  seeds_sf = NULL,
  features_sf = NULL,
  fill_col = NULL,
  palette = "viridis",
  na_fill = "grey90",
  tile_alpha = 0.9,
  outline_col = "white",
  outline_size = 0.2,
  features_col = "#333333",
  features_size = 0.5,
  seeds_col = "#1f77b4",
  seeds_size = 1.5,
  boundary_col = "#111111",
  boundary_size = 0.6,
  labels = FALSE,
  label_col = NULL,
  label_size = 2.7,
  legend = TRUE,
  legend_title = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  target_crs = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  expand = TRUE
)

Arguments

tessellation_sf

An sf POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON layer. Required.

boundary

Optional sf/sfc polygon outline layer.

seeds_sf

Optional sf/sfc point layer of seed locations.

features_sf

Optional sf/sfc layer of additional features.

fill_col

Name of the COLUMN in tessellation_sf to map to fill; NULL for no fill. A numeric column gets a continuous scale, as does a Date or POSIXct column (on a date or time axis) and a units or difftime column (drawn as numbers, with the unit in the legend title); anything else a discrete one. fill_col and label_col name columns, while outline_col, features_col, seeds_col and boundary_col are colours.

palette

Viridis palette, passed as option to ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c() or ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_d(): "viridis" (default), "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako" or "turbo".

na_fill

Fill for NA values. Default "grey90".

tile_alpha

Alpha for filled polygons. Default 0.9.

outline_col, outline_size

Colour and line width of the cell outlines. Defaults "white" and 0.2.

features_col, features_size

Colour and point size of the feature overlay. Defaults "#333333" and 0.5.

seeds_col, seeds_size

Colour and point size of the seed overlay. Defaults "#1f77b4" and 1.5.

boundary_col, boundary_size

Colour and line width of the boundary outline. Defaults "#111111" and 0.6.

labels

Logical; draw per-cell labels. Default FALSE. A cell is labelled when its label is not NA and it has a location; when no cell has both, the labels are skipped with a log line.

label_col

Name of the COLUMN holding the label text. Default NULL: the first of "poly_id", "polygon_id", "id", "cell_id" and "grid_id" the layer has, the order in which assign_features_to_polygons() reads a polygon layer's IDs, so the cells of build_tessellation() and the output of summarize_by_cell() are labelled without naming one, by the ID the summary is keyed on. A units or difftime column is drawn formatted, with its unit.

label_size

Label text size. Default 2.7.

legend

Logical; show fill legend. Default TRUE.

legend_title

Optional legend title.

theme

A ggplot2 theme. Default NULL, which uses ggplot2::theme_void().

target_crs

Optional CRS for plotting. When NULL (the default) the tessellation's own CRS is used, or (if the tessellation has none) a CRS borrowed from the first overlay that carries one, so a CRS-less grid drawn with located features still lines up. Any layer that arrives without a CRS is brought into the plot's CRS instead of being dropped: reprojected when its coordinates look like longitude/latitude, otherwise stamped with a warning, since a stamp assumes the coordinates were already in that CRS. A plot CRS in longitude and latitude is not stamped on coordinates that cannot be in it (an x outside -180 to 360, or a y beyond 90 north or south): the call stops and asks for the layer's CRS or a projected target_crs.

title, subtitle, caption

Plot annotations.

xlim, ylim

Optional numeric vectors of length 2 for coordinate limits (in the plot CRS). Default NULL (auto).

expand

Logical; expand plot area slightly beyond data limits. Default TRUE.

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Details

Every layer is drawn in x and y: a layer whose geometries mix XY with XYZ or XYM (as rbind() of an XY and an XYZ layer gives) is drawn without its Z and M. The labels are placed in x and y, also on cells whose geometries carry M (XYM or XYZM).

A row of any layer with a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150 has no location: it is left out of the map, with one warning that says how many rows of which argument were not drawn. A row the plot's CRS cannot place in full is drawn as the move leaves it (empty, or without the vertices it cannot place), with a warning of class spatialkit_rows_unplaced that names it.

See also

Other cell building: build_tessellation(), clip_target_for(), create_grid_polygons(), create_grid_polygons_cached(), create_voronoi_polygons(), ensure_stable_poly_id(), get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(), voronoi_seeds_random()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(sf)
  set.seed(1)
  n <- 60
  pts <- st_as_sf(
    data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),
               z = rnorm(n)),
    coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
  )
  # Cells from the points, the response aggregated onto them, and the map
  # shaded by the cell mean rather than by an arbitrary ID.  Each cell
  # holds one point, so there is nothing to pool: estimate = "mean".
  tess  <- build_tessellation(pts, method = "voronoi", quiet = TRUE)
  asg   <- assign_features_to_polygons(pts, tess$cells,
                                       polygon_id_col = "cell_id")
  cells <- summarize_by_cell(asg, response_var = "z", id_col = "cell_id",
                             cells_sf = tess$cells, estimate = "mean")
  plot_tessellation_map(cells, features_sf = pts, fill_col = "resp_mean_z",
                        legend_title = "mean z")
}
